overview: Draft covering the part common to both candidate designs: a review of ambulance patient care records against the pre-hospital tranexamic acid standard. The linked outcome component is described but not started unless the data-sharing agreement is renewed and the design is decided.
population: Adults attended by the regional ambulance service between January 2023 and June 2026 who met the tranexamic acid criteria (suspected major bleeding after injury within three hours), identified by the audit team from records.
exposure: Pathway delivery: tranexamic acid given or not, and time from injury to dose; crew configuration, patient age and transport time as descriptive factors.
procedures: The audit team searches the records database for injury incidents with the criteria recorded, a second reviewer checks eligibility for a random 10 percent, and each record is coded for administration, dose time, injury time (known or estimated) and reasons documented for not giving the drug. Results are presented at clinical governance meetings. If the agreement is renewed, a separate protocol amendment will set out linkage and outcome analysis.

outcomes.name: Eligible patients treated within three hours
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible patients given tranexamic acid within three hours of injury
outcomes.why: The pathway standard, and the timing that trial data say matters.

outcomes.name: Time from injury to dose
outcomes.measure: Median minutes from known or estimated injury time to administration

outcomes.name: Injury time documentation
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible records with a known rather than estimated injury time

outcomes.name: Doses given outside protocol
outcomes.measure: Proportion of doses given after three hours or to patients not meeting criteria
outcomes.why: Late or unnecessary doses carry risk without benefit.

feasibility: The audit team estimates about 450 eligible incidents over three and a half years and two days of review per 100 records within existing governance time.
biasMitigation: Eligibility checked by a second reviewer on a random 10 percent
Known and estimated injury times reported separately
No outcome claims without linked data

biasFlags.label: Eligibility from records
biasFlags.note: Crews may not record criteria when they decide not to give the drug.

biasFlags.label: Estimated injury time
biasFlags.note: Timing results are less certain for estimated times.

biasFlags.label: Selective linkage if outcomes are later added
biasFlags.note: Transfers and older patients match less often.

flags: Outcome component deferred rather than added
parsimony.simplestPath: One records review against one standard, reported descriptively.

theoreticalFramework: None; a standard-based audit needs no framework.
summary: Draft audit of ambulance records against the tranexamic acid standard; outcome component deferred.
